scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Mei Li and I'm 31. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?
Hi. I see you're asking about a refund. Can you tell me what the service was and provide the account number associated with it?
It's for the Premium Streaming subscription. My account number is 8849201.
Okay, thanks. I'm looking at the account now. Like you said, it's been 34 days since the cancellation. Our policy is 30 days, so I can't really do anything here. It's just the policy.
I understand the policy, but I was out of the country and had no access to my email or bank statements. Is there any way to make an exception given the circumstances?
I don't know, I guess I can just pass this to a supervisor since you're insisting. I'm going to escalate this to the billing department queue for you.
Oh, okay. Will they reach out to me via email, or do I need to call back?
I already told you I'm escalating it. You'll hear back eventually. Is there anything else?

escalation_reason: Agent failed to utilize tier-1 authority to review exception requests and instead deflected to a supervisor due to lack of engagement.

judge_scores.justification: The agent showed poor empathy by offering curt, dismissive responses and failed to make a genuine resolution effort within their authority, prematurely escalating the request. Furthermore, the agent communicated poorly regarding the next steps for the escalation, leaving the customer with vague answers.
